subject: [PATCH 2/3] mm/pagewalk: let folio_walk_start() run under the per-VMA lock

reviews.author: Lorenzo Stoakes
reviews.summary:
Reviewer questioned whether the patch description clearly states that interrupts must be disabled in addition to holding the per-VMA lock, and suggested making this explicit

Reviewer questioned the assumption that Khugepaged fixes the issue of concurrent munmap or THP collapse freeing page tables while a walker is active, and asked for clarification on how it addresses this problem.

The reviewer notes that pte_offset_map_lock() takes the RCU lock and then locklessly retrieves a pointer to the PTE page table, making it safe for folio_walk_start() to hold the per-VMA lock as long as interrupts are disabled until folio_walk_end().
sentiment_signals: clarified the safety of holding the per-VMA lock

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that a specific detail was missing and thanked Lorenzo for pointing it out, indicating no further revision is needed.
reviews.raw_body:
Ahhh! That's the part I was missing. Thank you.

That simplifies things nicely.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

2026-07-07.patch_summary: This patch allows callers of folio_walk_start() to run under the per-VMA lock instead of the mmap lock, reducing contention and improving performance for readers that only need to access a single page. The patch adds a new flag FW_VMA_LOCKED, which requires CONFIG_MMU_GATHER_RCU_TABLE_FREE and excludes hugetlb VMAs. Callers must keep interrupts disabled until folio_walk_end(). This change does not affect existing callers, as none currently pass the FW_VMA_LOCKED flag.
